measurements.strace_red_storm: kill sent +397ms; the tombstone fsync STALLS 652.7ms (fsync(15) 17.121823 -> resumed 17.774554; tombstone rename 17.774705); the submit fires +903ms INSIDE the stalled window; the daemon ACCEPTS it (success:true at 17.775406); the kill resolves +909ms; the worker dies mid-turn; the turn settles with NO rendered outcome; run exits Ok with the frozen Waiting frame; assert 4716 fails. Storm campaign: 1R/13G (the stall-probability of the regime).
measurements.natural_stall_evidence: a 627.7ms fsync stall observed naturally inside battery A's first run on kbfkp829 (create path) - the regime exists uninduced whenever writeback backs up (post-build/post-gate states).
measurements.lineage_at_pre_window_b89b8ffdd: the race contract is byte-identical PRE-window: the test's sleep(400ms) kill task + WaitMs(900) submit hold (test lines 4642/4702), the Kill handler's persist_stop_tombstone (routing.rs:401), and write_file_atomic's sync_all (descriptor.rs:230) all present at b89b8ffdd.

mechanism: The test's fixed wall-clock contract (Kill at +400ms, submit held to +900ms, 'long after the kill's stop resolved') races the daemon's Kill-path durability: persist_stop_tombstone (TS persistWorkerStopTombstone parity) fsyncs the descriptor BEFORE the stop is forwarded and BEFORE the Kill response returns. On fast I/O (CI: sub-ms fsyncs) the kill resolves ~490ms before the submit -> the session is already unknown -> the submit is refused -> submit_prompt returns Err -> the refused-submit contract renders (the TS onSubmit catch: showError + restore ladder). Under a stalled-fsync regime (VM writeback storms: 40ms p50 calm, 100-650ms stalls observed) the tombstone persist outlives the 500ms window -> the submit lands while the session is still live -> the daemon ACCEPTS it -> the turn goes active (the Waiting spinner) -> the kill lands mid-turn -> the worker dies -> the turn settles with no rendered outcome -> the run exits Ok and the assert fails with the frozen Waiting frame. The flip rate is the run's fsync-stall probability: 0 on CI, 1-2/6 warm-VM, 3/3 their post-gate-stalled VM, 1/14 under the induced storm.

validity.contamination_disclosed: the walk's runs are back-to-back with builds interleaved (writeback contamination - the first run after each build skews red); the batteries are the clean measurement (spaced, idle, uptime snapshots archived). Rerun discipline: 2 spaced runs per head per battery, no third rerun attempted; the counts are disclosed as flip rates, not rerun-to-green.
validity.single_red_trace: one induced red trace (trace-2) + one natural red class (their 3/3 + the batteries' 6 reds, all the identical 4716 signature) - the mechanism quote is from the induced red; the batteries' reds match the signature.

outcome: honest triage outcome: NO culprit commit. The 30808d2f4..c85b8e05b window attribution is FALSIFIED on four axes (the walk's endpoint inversion, the pre-window red at b89b8ffdd, the red at their own green head 24ef25d3c, the fresh-VM all-green control). The red is a STANDING, regime-gated test-side race: the test's +400/+900ms clock vs the Kill-path tombstone fsync, both the port's own code, byte-identical pre-window. The flagged suspects are exonerated structurally (#3002 test-only separate binary; #2735 footer-badge render - the red frames render the footer fine - with no Kill-path touch; #3014/#3018 test-mass splits).
decision: DISPOSITION FOR MERGE BARS/VM GATES: a red of this test on a VM is the standing environmental class (the I/O-regime-gated kill-vs-submit race), NOT a base regression and NOT window-caused; cite this record; CI (fast fsync) is the contract surface. The known_reds.json falsification annotation is superseded by this bisect outcome (annotated, not rescoped, per the operator's ruling). FIX ROUTING (both sides the port's own, pre-window; no product change made in this triage): (a) widen WaitMs(900) - pragmatic but green-fishing-adjacent alone (any regime stalling past the new margin re-flips); (b) a deterministic conditional submit barrier - today's plan vocabulary cannot see the kill (it produces no frame change), so it needs a kill-rendered frame signal or an external-condition wait step; (c) product-side: make an accepted-then-killed turn surface the error row + draft (a TS-parity question for mid-turn session death - separate lane's scope, disclosed). The concurrent_spawns investigation is untouched here (sibling lane's scope).
parity_notes: No frozen surface touched: this is a read-only triage (no code change, no PR). The mechanism analysis names TS-parity code (persistWorkerStopTombstone, the onSubmit catch ladder) as context, not as a change.
